2.  24-52113  Recommendation to approve partnership on YHSI Grant

  Alexa Dixson-Griggs, Administrative Coordinator introduced the item and the team
  that will present on the YHSI Grant.
  • LAHSA reached out to Long Beach to co-apply for the YHSI grant. Staff were
  interested and wanted to have the Board approve the co-application.
  • The Youth Team leading working on the grant application introduced
  themselves to the Board.
  • HUD announced a one-time system improvement fund for at-risk youth
  experiencing homelessness. The application was due Feb 15, 2023.
  • Due to limited time, the proposed application is for $800,000 to help fund the
  Youth Leadership Team.
  • The Youth Leadership Team will be a partnership across LA Emissary,
  HYFLA, and Long Beach Youth Council to enhance a cross system
  collaboration that helps design and implement youth-led needs assessment
  and an oversight and accountability mechanism. Both would help influence
  policy and funding changes as well as ensure progress is made on youth
  policies and funding priorities.
  • The Youth Leadership team set policy goals that the newly funded team
  would help accomplish. Some of which include reducing the number of exits
  from foster care into homelessness and at either one funding or policy
  priority that helps increase access to traditional or nontraditional mental
  health supports across LA County.
  • Through this project, Long Beach CoC will be able to add youth and young
  adult (YYA) representative to county-wide leadership table, provide
  additional trainings to YYA from Long Beach, have YYA participate in and
  facilitate trainings with County leaders, be provided compensation for YYA
  from Long Beach to participate in above activities, deepen collaboration
  between Long Beach YCES and LA YCES to reduce barriers and improve
  outcomes for YYA.
  • Board members had questions regarding the age range of the defined youth,
  budget considerations, expect program timelines and clarifications on roles
  and goals of the Youth Leadership Team.
  • Members of the team took turns answering.
  • Board Members also provide insight into other programming that could
  increase the scope of youth peer services. Grants like Cal Mesa could help
  support and grow the team to have further reach.
  • Members of the team thanked the Board for their time and guidance.

  A motion was made by Member Washington, seconded by Co-Chair Shuford,
